requirement: Build a scalable URL shortener service with APIs, persistence, and analytics.
engineering_problem: Design and build a new system to satisfy: "Build a scalable URL shortener service with APIs, persistence, and analytics." Scope capabilities: api, persistence, analytics, scalability. Open questions to settle first: vague term: 'scalable', scale target.

ambiguities.clarifying_question: What load must it handle (requests/sec, records, users) and over what time horizon?
ambiguities.default_assumption: Pick a conservative measurable target and confirm it.

ambiguities.clarifying_question: Expected peak requests/sec, total records, read:write ratio, growth rate?
ambiguities.default_assumption: Design for ~1k redirects/sec per instance and horizontal scale-out.

ambiguities.clarifying_question: Is there a mandated database, or operational constraints (managed service, no Docker)?
ambiguities.default_assumption: SQLite for the prototype behind an ORM, PostgreSQL for production.

ambiguities.issue: 'Analytics' can mean totals, time series, or segmentation.
ambiguities.clarifying_question: Which dimensions (time, referrer, device, geo, unique visitors), freshness and retention?
ambiguities.default_assumption: Totals, time series, referrer, device/browser/OS, country, unique visitors.

assumptions: Interface is a JSON/REST HTTP API with an OpenAPI contract.
A relational database is acceptable; schema evolves via migrations.
Analytics are near-real-time (seconds), aggregated per link, and identifiers are hashed for privacy.
Horizontal scaling of stateless instances behind a load balancer; numeric targets are to be confirmed.
Pick a conservative measurable target and confirm it.
Design for ~1k redirects/sec per instance and horizontal scale-out.
SQLite for the prototype behind an ORM, PostgreSQL for production.
Totals, time series, referrer, device/browser/OS, country, unique visitors.
Engineer reviews and owns all AI-generated output; nothing is accepted without running it.

tasks.title: Clarify requirements and record assumptions
tasks.description: Resolve open questions, define acceptance criteria and non-goals with the stakeholder.
tasks.ai_assist: Ask AI to list ambiguities and draft clarifying questions; engineer decides which answers are accepted.
tasks.validation: Acceptance criteria are written, measurable and signed off.

tasks.title: Design architecture and data/API contracts
tasks.description: Choose components, data model, API contract and key trade-offs; document decisions.
tasks.ai_assist: Use AI to compare design options and draft an OpenAPI/schema; engineer selects and justifies.
tasks.validation: Design review: every requirement maps to a component; trade-offs recorded.

tasks.title: Scaffold project, configuration and tooling
tasks.description: Project layout, dependency management, config via environment, lint/test tooling.
tasks.ai_assist: AI generates boilerplate; engineer prunes unused dependencies and checks versions exist.
tasks.validation: Clean checkout installs and runs the (empty) test suite.

tasks.title: Implement persistent storage layer
tasks.description: Schema, indexes, constraints and data-access code; migrations strategy.
tasks.ai_assist: AI drafts models and queries; engineer reviews indexes, constraints and transaction boundaries.
tasks.validation: Integration tests against a real database; data survives restart.

tasks.title: Implement core domain logic and API endpoints
tasks.description: Request validation, business rules, error model and endpoint handlers.
tasks.ai_assist: AI generates handlers and validators; engineer verifies edge cases and error semantics.
tasks.validation: Unit tests for rules; API tests for status codes and error bodies.

tasks.title: Implement event capture and analytics queries
tasks.description: Capture events off the hot path, enrich, aggregate by time and dimension.
tasks.ai_assist: AI drafts aggregation queries; engineer checks time-zone, bucketing and index use.
tasks.validation: Seeded-data tests with known aggregates; query plan check on large data.

tasks.title: Address scalability: statelessness, async work, limits
tasks.description: Keep app stateless, move slow work off the request path, identify bottlenecks.
tasks.ai_assist: AI proposes bottlenecks and fixes; engineer validates with measurements, not assumptions.
tasks.validation: Load test with stated target; document measured throughput and limits.

tasks.title: Write unit and integration tests
tasks.description: Cover rules, error paths, persistence and API contract; include negative and boundary cases.
tasks.ai_assist: AI drafts test cases and fixtures; engineer checks they would fail without the feature (no tautologies).
tasks.validation: Coverage report reviewed for meaningful branches; mutation spot-checks.

tasks.title: Security and performance review
tasks.description: Input validation, injection/SSRF/open-redirect, secrets handling, resource exhaustion, N+1 queries.
tasks.ai_assist: AI acts as reviewer producing a checklist; engineer triages and fixes findings.
tasks.validation: Checklist items closed or explicitly accepted as risks.

tasks.title: Write documentation and API reference
tasks.ai_assist: AI drafts docs from code; engineer verifies every command and example actually runs.
tasks.validation: A new reader can run and evaluate the solution from the README alone.

tasks.title: Produce final engineering summary
tasks.description: Approach, artifacts, risks, validation results, assumptions and limitations.
tasks.ai_assist: AI structures the summary; engineer owns every claim and its evidence.
tasks.validation: Each claim links to a test, measurement or code reference.

risks.risk: Ambiguous requirement leads to building the wrong thing.
risks.mitigation: Resolve blocking questions first; record assumptions; demo early.

risks.risk: Schema/index choices may not suit query patterns as data grows.
risks.mitigation: Model access patterns first; index for them; plan migrations (Alembic).

risks.risk: Concurrent writes can create duplicates or lose updates.
risks.mitigation: Use DB constraints and transactions; test concurrent paths.

risks.risk: Writing analytics synchronously on the request path adds latency and couples availability.
risks.mitigation: Queue events and batch-write; accept bounded loss or use a durable broker.

risks.risk: Privacy: raw IPs/user agents are personal data.
Scalability target is unquantified so the design may be over- or under-built.
risks.impact: Wasted effort or outage under load.
risks.mitigation: Agree numeric targets; load-test; document measured limits.

risks.risk: AI-generated code may contain hallucinated APIs, wrong library versions or subtle logic errors.
risks.impact: Runtime failures or incorrect behaviour that looks plausible.
risks.mitigation: Run everything; review each hunk; pin dependency versions; prefer small iterative prompts.

risks.risk: AI-generated tests can be shallow, tautological or mirror the implementation (coverage gaps).
risks.mitigation: Require negative/boundary cases, confirm tests fail without the change, review coverage by branch.

risks.risk: AI tends to over-engineer or pick inefficient patterns (N+1 queries, blocking I/O on hot paths).
risks.mitigation: Set explicit non-functional targets, profile/measure, simplify before accepting.

risks.risk: AI may suggest insecure defaults (hard-coded secrets, permissive validation).
risks.mitigation: Security checklist review, secrets via environment, adversarial tests for inputs.

tradeoffs: SQLite is zero-setup but single-writer; PostgreSQL scales better at the cost of operating a server.
Asynchronous event capture keeps the hot path fast but can lose in-flight events on a crash; durable queues cost complexity.
Stateless instances scale horizontally, but per-process caches/limiters then need shared backends.
